stem.text: Consider the polar curve \( r = 3 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} + 6 \) for \( 0.1 \le \theta \le 1.75 \). Using a calculator, find the value of \( \theta \) that corresponds to the point on the curve farthest from the y-axis. Justify your answer, show the setup, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The distance from the y-axis is \( |x| \), where \( x = r\cos\theta = \left(3 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} + 6\right) \cos{\left(\theta \right)} \).

Set \( \frac{dx}{d\theta} = - \left(3 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} + 6\right) \sin{\left(\theta \right)} + 3 \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} = 0 \). On the interval a calculator gives one solution, \( \theta \approx 0.375 \).

Compare the candidates, the critical angle and both endpoints: \( |x(0.1)| \approx 6.268 \), \( |x(0.375)| \approx 6.606 \), \( |x(1.75)| \approx 1.596 \). The largest distance is at \( \theta \approx 0.375 \), so that is the farthest point.

options.derivation: the candidates comparison run without the interior critical angle, so the farther endpoint is reported
the candidates compared correctly but the one nearest the axis reported
r treated as the distance from the axis, so the angle where r is largest is reported
